To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a conditional term rewriting system R is logically equivalent to the conditional equational system generated by R if R is oriented and satisfies one of the following conditions: (1) R is a left-linear conditional term rewriting system and R is terminating; or (2) R is a right-linear conditional term rewriting rule and R is confluent; or (3) R is a linear conditional term rewriting system.

the following conditions are sufficient for logicality of oriented conditional term systems: (1) the conditional equations are of the form $x \leftarrow y \rightarrow z$, (2) the conditional equations have no solutions, (3) all equations have at least one solution, (4) the equations are oriented, (5) the equations are of the forms $x \leftleftarrows y$, $x \leftarrows y$ or $x \leftrightarrow y$, and (6)

1) a conditional term rewriting system R is logical if the set of its ground instances is a conservative extension of a ground equational system, and 2) a conditional term oriented term rewriting system R (that is, an oriented conditional term rewriting system where all the conditional rules have the same orientation) is logical if it has a ground instance that is a conservative extension (in the sense of equational logic) of a ground equi- tational system.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
an oriented conditional term rewriting system with a non-orientable underlying equational system is logical if the set of ground terms is finite.
an oriented conditional term rewriting system with a finite set of rules is logical if and only if it is confluent.
a conditional term rewriting system with a finite number of rewrite rules is logical if the underlying conditional equa-tional system is.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a conditional term rewriting system has a logical model if and only if the underlying conditional equa-tional system has a logical one.
a conditional term rewriting system has a logical semantics if the corresponding oriented conditional term rewriting system does.
the class of oriented systems is closed under the following operations: union, intersection, composition, and inverse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the logicality of oriented conditional systems is closely related to the existence of an oriented term rewriting system that is logically equivalent to the given one.
